text:
alex: Heads-up — canary deploy (svc-prod-canary) completed ~10m ago but I'm not seeing any KMS decrypt entries in the audit logs for the service account that handled the traffic. I expected at least 'Decrypt' events for key redwood-prod-ops.

maria: deploy-bot posted a message from the deploy run?

deploy-bot: deploy finished: canary=svc-prod-canary, version=2026.03.23-8b2f, status=success, tasks=12

jun: alex, can you paste the exact service account and the timeframe? I can query CloudAudit logs.

alex: svc-buildbot-prod, timeframe ~1723456700-1723456750. I looked via kibana and nothing for key redwood-prod-ops.decrypt during that window. There are other KMS events earlier today.

sam: quick Q: did the RBAC change to the keystore happen as part of this rollout? I remember a PR earlier that revoked a group binding for infra:canary-workers.

maria: yes we merged infra/keystore: PR#4821 yesterday. It replaced a broad binding with a narrower one for the new pool. That should be fine but maybe the new binding wasn't granted to svc-buildbot-prod.

jun: running audit query now: ```gcloud logging read 'resource.type="k8s_container" AND protoPayload.methodName:"Decrypt" AND timestamp>="2026-03-23T15:00:00Z"' --project=redwood-prod --limit=50```

jun: result: 0 hits in that window. There are hits at 14:30 and 15:20 though.

alex: interesting — traffic definitely hit the canary backend (latency traces show requests routed). Two possible hypotheses: 1) the service fell back to cached plaintext (bad), 2) requests were handled by a pod with different identity (sa mismatch), or 3) our KMS audit exporter had a gap.

maria: also saw a SAST alert popped on the canary image build earlier: `proto/parser.go: potential unchecked error` — low severity but flipping RBAC + unchecked crypto ops is worth a look. Not sure related.

ir-oncall: tagging incident channel just in case. If KMS decrypt calls aren't being recorded that's an integrity issue. Suggest capture: kube describe of current pods, service-account binding, and the node identity.

alex: I grabbed the pod and SA: 
```
kubectl get pods -l app=svc-prod-canary -o wide
kubectl describe pod svc-prod-canary-7f8d
kubectl get serviceaccount svc-buildbot-prod -o yaml
```

sam: copy. Also check IAM policy binding for the key: `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy redwood-prod-ops --location=global --keyring=prod-keyring`

jun: IAM binding shows `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` assigned to `serviceAccount:svc-buildbot-prod@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` in the policy. So binding exists.

alex: but the pod's identity looks like `svc-buildbot-canary-ephemeral` not `svc-buildbot-prod`. So it might be using a different SA due to our deployment template fallback.

maria: that explains no KMS logs under svc-buildbot-prod. Where do logs for the ephemeral SA show up? Jun, can you query for any Decrypt entries from svc-buildbot-canary-ephemeral?

jun: querying... small result set: there are 3 Decrypt events at 1723456725 attributed to `svc-buildbot-canary-ephemeral@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com`. They match the canary time. So KMS is being called and logged, but under a different identity.

alex: ok so probably a rollout artifact: the canary pod got the ephemeral SA instead of the intended production SA. That still means audit logs exist but our automation expected svc-buildbot-prod entries. Need to update alerting and docs.

maria: action items: 1) infra to confirm pod template SA mapping for canary, 2) update the KMS audit query dashboards to include ephemeral SA patterns, 3) follow up on SAST finding in the build to ensure crypto paths handle errors.

sam: for immediate mitigation, I can patch the deployment to explicitly set `serviceAccountName: svc-buildbot-prod` for the canary to align identities. Want me to push?

alex: do it, but be careful — we rolled the narrower IAM binding intentionally. If the prod SA doesn't have necessary access in the keyring due to the PR we merged, patching might cause real denies. Confirm binding before patch.

jun: binding exists for the prod SA (I checked) so patching is safe. If anyone is oncall for infra do the patch and watch KMS logs.

ir-oncall: I'm oncall, will monitor. Also recommend we open a short postmortem note: 'canary SA drift -> audit alert gap / SAST triage linkage' and tag SecOps + Infra.

maria: created ticket SEC-2026: include audit query snippets, pod YAML, and the build SAST link. Will add triage owner and timeline.

alex: thanks all. Once the pod identity is fixed, we'll re-run the end-to-end and confirm KMS Decrypt logs show up in our dashboards and the SAST low finding will be assigned to the build team for review. :thumbsup:

sam: patch applied, rolling 2 pods, monitoring logs. :eyes:

jun: I see three Decrypt hits from prod SA now at 1723456798. Closing the loop from my side.

alex: closing here — moving the follow-ups to SEC-2026.
